avoid.added.en: Added to the never-avoid list. Grass may grow inside anything matching {pattern}.

avoid.asking.note: Object dialogue: the verdict box while the engine is asked.

avoid.canopy_added.en: Added to {name}. Grass cards that use this canopy are placed under, or kept clear of, anything matching {pattern}.
avoid.canopy_added.note: Object dialogue, canopies: said when a pattern is added to a canopy.

avoid.canopy_choose.note: Object dialogue, canopies: said when Add is pressed with no canopy chosen.

avoid.canopy_hint.en: Grass cards that use this canopy are placed under, or kept clear of, anything matching this (id or mesh, * matches anything after it).

avoid.canopy_hint_title.en: Matched against the object id, the mesh path and its file name. * matches anything after it, so flora_tree_ai* covers a whole family.

avoid.canopy_new.note: The object dialogue, the last entry of the canopy picker.

avoid.canopy_remove.note: The object dialogue, the button beside a canopy this mesh is part of.

avoid.canopy_remove_title.en: Removes the pattern {pattern} from {name}. Every mesh it matched is removed from the canopy too.
avoid.canopy_remove_title.note: The object dialogue, hovering that button.

avoid.canopy_took_off.note: Object dialogue, canopies: said when a pattern is removed from a canopy.

avoid.canopy_unnamed.note: The object dialogue, how a canopy with no name is listed.

avoid.canopy_verdict_any.en: Cards that use any canopy still count it if it hangs over the ground.
avoid.canopy_verdict_any.note: The object dialogue, the plain text after that verdict.

avoid.canopy_verdict_by.note: The object dialogue, after the canopy's name in that verdict; {pattern} is the one that matched.

avoid.canopy_verdict_first.en: There are no canopies yet. Adding this mesh creates the first one.
avoid.canopy_verdict_first.note: The object dialogue, the plain text after that verdict while the rules file has no canopies.

avoid.canopy_verdict_in.note: The object dialogue, the canopy verdict when a canopy's pattern matches this mesh; {name} is the canopy's.

avoid.canopy_verdict_none.note: The object dialogue, the canopy verdict when no canopy's pattern matches this mesh.

avoid.clear_failed.note: Object dialogue: said when a clear failed.

avoid.clear_model.en: Clear all paint from all meshes of this type

avoid.clear_model_body.en: Every reference in the world using {mesh}, not just this one, and not just the ones you can see. Undo can bring the paint back while the program is open.
avoid.clear_model_body.note: That dialogue's body; {mesh} is the mesh file name, bold.

avoid.clear_model_head.en: Clear the paint on every object of this type?
avoid.clear_model_head.note: The dialogue before clearing the paint on every reference of a mesh: its title.

avoid.clear_model_title.en: Removes all paint from every reference in the world using this mesh. Undoable.

avoid.clear_model_yes_note.note: The note under the confirming choice.

avoid.clear_ref.en: Clear all paint from this reference

avoid.clear_ref_body.en: All paint on this one reference. The grass rules are untouched, and Undo can bring the paint back while the program is open.

avoid.clear_ref_head.en: Clear the paint on this object?
avoid.clear_ref_head.note: The dialogue before clearing the paint on one reference: its title.

avoid.clear_ref_title.en: Removes all paint from this one reference. Undoable.

avoid.clear_ref_yes_note.note: The note under the confirming choice.

avoid.cleared_n.one.note: Object dialogue: said after clearing the paint on every reference of a mesh (one).

avoid.cleared_n.other.note: Object dialogue: said after clearing the paint on every reference of a mesh.

avoid.cleared_ref.note: Object dialogue: said after the paint on this reference was cleared.

avoid.compact_failed.note: Object dialogue: said when Compact failed.

avoid.compact_title.en: Each mesh can only take a set amount of paint (a limitation due to performance). This option drops paint marks that mostly repeat ones already there. Fewer marks with almost the same result, but fine detail can soften where strokes overlap. Undoable.

avoid.compacted.note: Object dialogue: said after Compact thins the paint on this reference.

avoid.door_open.note: The object dialogue, the green button on a teleporting door that loads the cell on the far side.

avoid.door_open_title.en: Load {cell}, the cell this door leads to
avoid.door_open_title.note: The object dialogue, the door button's tooltip; {cell} is the destination's name.

avoid.edit_mesh_title.en: Open this object's mesh in the editor to assign rules to its textures and paint its own layer. What you set up applies to every placement of it.

avoid.list_add.note: Left column, the never-avoid and never-paint lists: the button that adds an empty row.

avoid.list_added.note: Toast after the copy/paste dialogue appended to a pattern list.

avoid.list_io.note: Left column, both pattern lists: the button that opens the copy/paste dialogue.

avoid.list_io_head.note: The never-avoid list's copy/paste dialogue: its heading.

avoid.list_io_hint.en: One pattern per line. * matches anything after it, and a pattern is tested against both the object id and its mesh path.
avoid.list_io_hint.note: The never-avoid list's copy/paste dialogue: the hint over the text area.

avoid.list_io_title.en: Copy these patterns, or paste a set in
avoid.list_io_title.note: Both pattern lists: the copy/paste button's tooltip.

avoid.list_replaced.note: Toast after the copy/paste dialogue replaced a pattern list.

avoid.never_ref_note.en: Only this specific reference. Other instances are not affected by this option.

avoid.never_ref_title.en: When on, grass grows through this one reference as if it were not there

avoid.no_verdict.note: Object dialogue: the verdict box when the engine could not answer.

avoid.nopaint_added.en: The brush will no longer land on anything matching {pattern}.
avoid.nopaint_added.note: Object dialogue: said when a pattern joins the never-paint list.

avoid.nopaint_hint.en: The brush will not land on anything matching this.

avoid.nopaint_hint_title.en: Patterns are matched against the object id, the mesh path and its file name. * matches anything that comes after.

avoid.nopaint_remove.note: The object dialogue, that button when the mesh is already on the never-accept-paint list.

avoid.nopaint_remove_note.en: Removing the pattern above from the never-paint-on list lets the brush land on this mesh again.

avoid.nopaint_removed.en: This mesh can take paint again.
avoid.nopaint_removed.note: Object dialogue: said when the mesh is taken off the never-paint list.

avoid.nothing_to_clear.note: Object dialogue: said when a clear found no paint.

avoid.paint_none.en: Currently no paint on this mesh.

avoid.paint_ref_note.en: Only this specific reference. Other instances are not affected by this option.

avoid.paint_verdict_never.en: Nothing can be painted on this mesh.
avoid.paint_verdict_never.note: The object dialogue, the paint verdict when a never-paint pattern covers this mesh.

avoid.paint_verdict_ok.en: This mesh can be painted on.
avoid.paint_verdict_ok.note: The object dialogue, the paint verdict when the brush may land here.

avoid.paint_verdict_ref.en: This reference does not take paint.
avoid.paint_verdict_ref.note: The object dialogue, the paint verdict when the switch below has turned this one reference off.

avoid.paint_why_never.en: It matches {pattern} on the never-paint-on list.
avoid.paint_why_never.note: Paint verdict: the reason when the mesh matches a never-paint pattern. {pattern} is bold.

avoid.paint_why_ref.en: The switch below has turned paint off for this one reference. Other references using this mesh still take paint.
avoid.paint_why_ref.note: Paint verdict: the reason while the per-reference paint switch is off.

avoid.painted.note: Object dialogue, the paint section: how many marks this reference carries. {marks} is the bold count, {room} the "of N" clause or nothing.

avoid.painted_of.note: Object dialogue, the paint section: the clause giving the room for marks on this reference.

avoid.pattern_hint.en: Grass may scatter clipping and inside anything matching this.

avoid.pattern_hint_title.en: Matched against the object id, the mesh path and its file name. * stands for any run of characters, so Flora_BC_* covers a whole family.

avoid.placed_by.note: Object dialogue: under the heading, which plugin placed the object.

avoid.ref_avoid_off.en: Avoidance now ignores this one reference.
avoid.ref_avoid_off.note: Object dialogue: said when the per-reference Never avoid switch is turned on.

avoid.ref_avoid_on.note: Object dialogue: said when the per-reference Never avoid switch is turned off.

avoid.ref_paint_off.en: The brush will no longer land on this reference.
avoid.ref_paint_off.note: Object dialogue: said when the per-reference paint switch is turned off.

avoid.ref_paint_on.note: Object dialogue: said when the per-reference paint switch is turned on.

avoid.remove.note: Never-avoid dialogue, the button when it will remove the pattern instead.

avoid.remove_note.en: Removing it makes grass avoid this object again.

avoid.removed.en: Removed from the never-avoid list. Grass avoids it again.
avoid.removed.note: Object dialogue: said when the pattern is taken off the never-avoid list.

avoid.type_pattern.note: Object dialogue: said when Add is pressed with an empty pattern.

avoid.v_actor.en: It is a living actor. It walks away from where the plugin put it, so a permanent hole in the grass under its starting spot would be wrong.

avoid.v_by_bounds.en: It has no collision in game, so it is tested against a box half the size of its bounds, enough to keep grass off the plant itself but not off every leaf it spreads
avoid.v_by_bounds.note: Avoidance verdict: how the shape was tested — a half-bounds box.

avoid.v_by_box.en: Its mesh has too many triangles to test against every blade, so it is tested against its bounding box
avoid.v_by_box.note: Avoidance verdict: how the shape was tested — the bounding box.

avoid.v_by_hull.note: Avoidance verdict: how the shape was tested — its collision hull.

avoid.v_by_shape.note: Avoidance verdict: how the shape was tested, when the engine did not say which way.

avoid.v_by_visible.en: Tested against its visible mesh, since it has no collision hull
avoid.v_by_visible.note: Avoidance verdict: how the shape was tested — the visible mesh.

avoid.v_clearance.en: , plus {n} units of clearance measured out from its surface
avoid.v_clearance.note: Avoidance verdict: the clearance clause inside the radius bracket.

avoid.v_corpse.en: It is a body, and Corpses is switched off.
avoid.v_corpse.note: Avoidance verdict: a corpse while Corpses is off.

avoid.v_excluded.en: It matches {pattern} on the never-avoid list.
avoid.v_excluded.note: Avoidance verdict: the object matches a never-avoid pattern. {pattern} is shown bold.

avoid.v_marker.en: It is an editor marker (a travel destination, a door target or the north arrow). The game never draws it, so grass grows straight through.
avoid.v_marker.note: Avoidance verdict: the object is an editor marker.

avoid.v_mesh_missing.en: It names a mesh that is not in the load order at all, most likely a mod that forgot to ship it.
avoid.v_mesh_missing.note: Avoidance verdict: the object's mesh file is missing.

avoid.v_no.note: Object dialogue, the avoidance verdict: the amber ruling, followed by the reason.

avoid.v_no_geometry.en: The mesh has no geometry to build a shape from. Either unreadable, or an effect with nothing solid in it.
avoid.v_no_geometry.note: Avoidance verdict: the mesh holds nothing solid.

avoid.v_off.en: Avoid objects is switched off, so nothing on the map is blocking grass.
avoid.v_off.note: Avoidance verdict: the reason when Avoid objects is off.

avoid.v_ref_off.en: Never avoid is on for this one reference, so avoidance ignores it and grass may grow where it stands. Other references using this mesh are still avoided.
avoid.v_ref_off.note: Avoidance verdict: the reason while the per-reference Never avoid switch is on.

avoid.v_shape_tail.en: {how} (radius {size} units{clearance}). Any grass still growing through it is outside the shape.
avoid.v_shape_tail.note: Avoidance verdict: the green reason. {how} is one of the "Tested against" strings, {clearance} the clearance clause or nothing.

avoid.v_too_small.en: Its collision shape has a radius of {size} units where it stands, under the "ignore under" setting of {min}. Lower that to keep grass off it.
avoid.v_too_small.note: Avoidance verdict: the object is under the ignore-under size.

avoid.v_unknown.en: Nothing in the load order says what this object looks like, so there is no shape to keep grass off.
avoid.v_unknown.note: Avoidance verdict: no record describes the object.

avoid.v_yes.note: Object dialogue, the avoidance verdict: the green ruling, followed by the reason.

avoid.wide_across.note: That warning's meshes clause; {list} names up to six, {more} is the "and N more" tail or nothing.

avoid.wide_body.en: {pattern} matches {n} object(s) in the cells you have loaded{across}. Removing it puts grass back around all of them.
avoid.wide_body.note: That warning's body. {pattern} is the pattern in code style, {n} the bold count, {across} the meshes clause or nothing.

avoid.wide_head.en: This pattern covers more than this object.
avoid.wide_head.note: Object dialogue: the bold lead of the warning when removing a wildcard pattern would reach other objects.

avoid.wide_more.note: That warning's tail when more than six meshes match.

browse.edited.note: The asset browser: the switch that shows only meshes with a setup.

browse.edited_title.en: Show only meshes that carry a setup (texture rules, their own paint, or a lock)

browse.fav_failed.note: Toast when starring an entry could not be saved.

browse.grass.note: The asset browser: the switch that shows only Meshes\grass.

browse.grass_title.en: Show only what is under Meshes\grass

browse.grid_title.en: Thumbnails, so you can pick by what it looks like
browse.grid_title.note: The asset browser: the grid view button's tooltip.

browse.head_mesh.note: The asset browser's heading for meshes.

browse.head_texture.note: The asset browser's heading for textures.

browse.indexing.note: The asset browser while the index is being built.

browse.list_title.en: One entry a line, with its whole path
browse.list_title.note: The asset browser: the list view button's tooltip.

browse.more.en: {n} of {total}. Keep scrolling for the rest.
browse.more.note: The asset browser: the note at the bottom of a long list.

browse.n_found.note: The asset browser's pill before a filter is typed.

browse.n_selected.note: The asset browser's footer: how many entries are ticked.

browse.none_edited.en: No set-up mesh matches. Nothing edited yet?
browse.none_edited.note: The asset browser, Edited on, when nothing matches.

browse.none_found.en: No assets found. Is Meshes/ present?
browse.none_found.note: The asset browser when the install has no assets.

browse.none_grass.en: Nothing under Meshes\grass matches that filter.
browse.none_grass.note: The asset browser, Grass folder on, when nothing matches.

browse.star_off_title.en: Star this, to keep it at the top of every picker of this kind
browse.star_off_title.note: The star on a picker row: its tooltip while not starred.

browse.star_on_title.en: Starred. Kept at the top of every picker of this kind
browse.star_on_title.note: The star on a picker row: its tooltip while starred.

busy.building_grass.note: The busy card while the grass is built for drawing.

busy.building_terrain.note: The busy card while the terrain is built.

busy.cancel.note: The button under the loading bar that stops a running export.

busy.drawing_scene.note: The connect's busy card, while the viewport rebuilds after the world has been read.

busy.gen_at.note: The same, naming the cell being scattered; {at} is its name or its grid.

busy.gen_cells.note: Under the export's bar, while it works; {n} is how many cells are done.

busy.generating.note: The busy overlay while a plugin is generated.

busy.indexing.note: The busy overlay's second line: reading the plugins and listing the assets.

busy.loading_cell.note: The busy card over the viewport while a cell loads.

busy.n_of.note: Under the busy card's heading: progress through a count.

busy.n_of_meshes.note: Under "Placing objects": progress through the meshes.

busy.placing_objects.note: The busy card while the objects are placed.

busy.reading_install.note: The busy overlay while a setup is connected.

busy.reading_map.note: The connect's busy card, while the cell picker's map is read ahead, before its cell count is known.

busy.reading_map_n.note: The connect's busy card, while the cell picker's map is read ahead: {done} and {total} are cell counts.

busy.reading_meshes.note: The connect's busy card, while every mesh is fingerprinted for the retextures panel and the texture grid, before the mesh count is known.

busy.reading_meshes_n.note: The connect's busy card, while every mesh is fingerprinted: {done} and {total} are mesh counts.

busy.resolving_overlay.note: The busy overlay's second line: working out which mod folders win.

busy.scattering.note: The busy card, and the bottom bar, while grass is scattered.

busy.scattering_sub.note: The bottom bar's form of that with progress; {sub} is "cell 3 of 9".

busy.stopping.en: stopping at the end of this cell…
busy.stopping.note: Under the export's bar once Cancel has been confirmed.

busy.walking_cells.note: The busy overlay's second line while a plugin is generated.

busy.writing_files.note: The busy overlay while the generated plugin is written to the folder you chose.

canopy.add.note: Left column, the button that adds a canopy.

canopy.add_pattern.note: Left column, the button that adds a pattern to a canopy.

canopy.add_pattern_title.en: Patterns match against the object id, the mesh path and its file name. * matches anything that comes after, e.g. flora_tree_ai*. Used on grass cards to stand only under it, or to keep clear of it. Saved in the rules file.
canopy.add_pattern_title.note: The Add pattern button's tooltip (18ft, asked for in the sheet).

canopy.add_title.note: That button's tooltip (round 18fk, Robin's wording review).

canopy.drop_title.en: Remove this canopy. Cards that used it have no canopy until pointed elsewhere.
canopy.drop_title.note: Left column, hovering a canopy's delete cross.

canopy.hint.en: Group meshes that hang over the ground (trees, mushrooms, bridges etc.) as canopies. (patterns; * matches anything)
canopy.hint.note: Left column, under the Canopies heading.

canopy.name_ph.note: Left column, the placeholder of a canopy's name field.

canopy.pattern_ph.note: Left column, Canopies: a pattern field's placeholder (an example pattern).

canopy.pattern_ph_title.en: Patterns match against the object id, the mesh path and its file name. * matches anything that comes after, e.g. flora_tree_ai*. Used on grass cards to stand only under it, or to keep clear of it. Saved in the rules file.
canopy.pattern_ph_title.note: A canopy pattern field's tooltip (18ft, asked for in the sheet).

canopy.title.note: Left column, the heading of the Canopies section (round 18k).

card.an_empty_slot.note: The copy toast's {name} when the card has neither mesh nor id.

card.browse_title.en: Browse meshes in your Data Files folder
card.browse_title.note: A grass card: the "…" button's tooltip beside the mesh field.

card.canopy.note: A grass card, the canopy row.

card.canopy_add.note: A grass card, the button that adds another canopy rule to it.

card.canopy_clear.note: A grass card, the canopy picker: clear of a named canopy.

card.canopy_clear_any.note: A grass card, the canopy picker: nothing hanging over.

card.canopy_drop.note: A grass card, hovering the cross beside one of its canopy rules.

card.canopy_gone.en: a canopy that no longer exists
card.canopy_gone.note: A grass card, the canopy picker when the card names a canopy the set has lost.

card.canopy_tip.en: Scatters only under the canopies named in the left column, or only clear of them, or under (or clear of) anything that hangs over the ground. Add as many rules as you like. They all apply, so one "clear of" keeps this mesh out however many it stands under. A canopy is a mesh's visible faces above the spot: a tree's crown, not its trunk.
card.canopy_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the canopy label.

card.canopy_under.note: A grass card, the canopy picker: under a named canopy.

card.canopy_under_any.note: A grass card, the canopy picker: under anything that hangs over.

card.copied.note: Toast after copying a grass card; {name} is its id or mesh.

card.copy_title.en: Copy this grass card, to paste into another rule
card.copy_title.note: A grass card: the copy button's tooltip.

card.curve.note: A grass card, the curvature row.

card.curve_tip.en: How far the ground sits below or above the ground around it, in units. Negative is a hollow, positive a ridge. Measured at the rule's curvature radius. Blank is no gate on this mesh.
card.curve_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the curvature label.

card.del_body.en: {name} at weight {weight}. The other slots keep their weights, so the ones left take a larger share.

card.del_head.note: The dialogue before deleting a grass card: its title.

card.del_title.note: A grass card: the delete button's tooltip.

card.drift_alone.en: This rule has only this card, so drifting changes nothing. Add another card first.
card.drift_alone.note: A grass card, under the Drifts switch when the rule has a single card.

card.drift_cover.note: A grass card, the Drifts section, the coverage row.

card.drift_cover_tip.en: Percent of the ground the patches cover. Low is a rare drift, high is this mesh nearly everywhere with clearings.
card.drift_cover_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the how much label under Drifts.

card.drift_edge.note: A grass card, the Drifts section, the edge softness row.

card.drift_edge_tip.en: 0 is a hard edge: this mesh or none. 100 fades out, so the patch thins into the rest of the rule instead of stopping.
card.drift_edge_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the edge label under Drifts.

card.drift_edit.note: The undo step's name when a grass card's drift settings change: “change a grass card’s drifts”.

card.drift_hint.en: Gathers this mesh into patches instead of spreading it evenly through the rule. It does not change how much grass grows. Inside a patch this card wins a larger share of the positions, outside it the rule's other cards do.
card.drift_hint.note: A grass card, at the top of the Drifts section.

card.drift_note.note: A grass card, beside the Drifts heading when the section is folded and drifting is on.

card.drift_on.note: A grass card, the switch in the Drifts section.

card.drift_size.note: A grass card, the Drifts section, the size row.

card.drift_size_tip.en: Units across a typical patch. Anchored to the world, so a patch runs across a cell border and stays put while you tune the spacing.
card.drift_size_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the patch size label under Drifts.

card.drift_warp.note: A grass card, the Drifts section, the warp row.

card.drift_warp_tip.en: 0 is round blobs, 100 is ragged outlines.
card.drift_warp_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the ragged label under Drifts.

card.empty.note: A grass card: the switch that makes the slot take positions and place nothing.

card.empty_note.en: Takes a position and places nothing. Leaves gaps without changing the spacing.
card.empty_note.note: A grass card: the note under Empty / Placeholder while it is on.

card.facing.note: A grass card, the facing row (round 18p).

card.facing_tip.en: Which way the ground faces where this mesh may stand: a compass heading (0 north, 90 east) and how far either side of it counts. Ground too flat to have a facing always passes. Blank is no gate on this mesh.
card.facing_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the facing label.

card.height.note: A grass card, Conditions: the ground-height pair's label.

card.height_tip.en: Ground height, in units, this mesh keeps between. The rule's other meshes scatter outside it. Blank inherits the rule's.
card.height_tip.note: A grass card, Conditions: the ground-height pair's tooltip.

card.mesh.note: A grass card: the mesh field's label.

card.mesh_not_installed.en: This mesh is not in your install.
card.mesh_not_installed.note: A grass card's swatch tooltip when the mesh is missing and the engine gave no reason.

card.mesh_ph.note: A grass card: the mesh field's placeholder (an example path).

card.n_set.note: A grass card: the count on a folded Overrides or Conditions heading.

card.name_ph.note: A grass card, the placeholder of its name field.

card.name_tip.en: What you call this card. Its own name, not its mesh's. The stands-with picker on the other cards lists these names.
card.name_tip.note: A grass card, hovering its name field.

card.near.note: A grass card, the near objects row (round 18k).

card.near_tip.en: Lowest and highest distance, in units, from the nearest object grass keeps clear of. Blank is the rule's, and this only tightens it.
card.near_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the near objects label.

card.object.note: A grass card: the label of the object-id field, under the mesh row.

card.object_note.en: {kind}: {name}, from {from}. Its references go into the Objects .esp.
card.object_note.note: A grass card: the note under an object-id card that the load order defines. {kind} is the kind word, {name} the record's name or id, {from} the plugin that last defines it.

card.object_note_grass.en: {kind}: {name}, from {from}. Its mesh is in the grass folder, so it is groundcover and goes into the groundcover .esp.
card.object_note_grass.note: A grass card: the note under an object-id card that is a static from the grass folder (round 18fy). Placeholders as card.object_note.

card.object_ph.en: or an object from the load order, by id
card.object_ph.note: A grass card: the object-id field's placeholder.

card.object_pick.note: A grass card: the button that opens the object picker.

card.object_pick_title.en: Pick a static, an activator, a creature or a leveled creature from your load order. The card is then that object rather than a mesh, and its references go into the Objects .esp on export
card.object_pick_title.note: A grass card: the object picker button's tooltip.

card.object_unknown_note.en: Nothing in the load order defines {id}. Check the id, or connect the setup that has it.
card.object_unknown_note.note: A grass card: the note under an object-id card no plugin defines.

card.object_unknown_title.en: No record with this id in the load order
card.object_unknown_title.note: A grass card: the tag's tooltip when the object id is unknown.

card.scale.note: A grass card, Overrides: the scale range's label.

card.scale_tip.en: The size range this mesh is drawn at. Blank inherits the rule’s.
card.scale_tip.note: A grass card, Overrides: the scale range's tooltip.

card.sec_conditions.note: A grass card, the heading of the folded section of settings that refuse ground.

card.sec_drift.note: A grass card, the heading of the folded section where this mesh gathers into patches (round 18ac).

card.sec_overrides.note: A grass card, the heading of the folded section of settings that replace the rule's.

card.shore.note: A grass card, the shoreline row, shown while the rule's shoreline band is on.

card.shore_band.note: A grass card, the shoreline band row.

card.shore_band_tip.en: How far from the water's edge this mesh may scatter, in units. Negative is under water. Blank is no gate on this mesh, and the rule's own band still holds.
card.shore_band_tip.note: A grass card, hovering the shoreline band label.

card.shore_off.note: A grass card, the shoreline picker: keeps the random yaw.

card.shore_on.note: A grass card, the shoreline picker: lies along the waterline.

card.shore_rule.note: A grass card, the shoreline picker's first entry; {how} is what the rule does.

card.shore_tip.en: Whether this mesh lies along the shore instead of spinning at random, and how far it is turned on top. The first entry is the rule's. The turn is in degrees, blank is the rule's.

intro.then.en:
Then open a .toml, import an .ini, or add a rule, and pick a ground texture on the left. Simplified previews the selected rule on a test patch. Real cell draws every rule that matches the ground in that cell, which is what the export does.

Terrain shape, ground height, patch size and the ban strip are preview stand-ins. The generator reads your landscape instead. Everything under Obstacle avoidance changes the .esp. Everything under Preview changes only what you are shown.

A color is attached to a rule, not to its name, so renaming the rule or changing its ground texture changes nothing here. Pointing the color at a different rule changes what grows on everything you have painted with it.

Moving it to another layer takes the ground painted with it along. Where that layer already has a color on the same spot, this one wins.

paint.swatch_clear_view_body.en: Every mark of {label} on {where}, both the ground and the objects there. The color itself stays on its layer, and so does its paint elsewhere.
paint.swatch_clear_view_body.note: The clear-in-view dialogue's body for a rule colour; {label} is the colour, {where} the cells.

paint.swatch_clear_view_note.en: its paint is removed from the loaded cells. The color itself stays
paint.swatch_clear_view_note.note: Under the clear-in-view option of a rule colour.

paint.swatch_move_note.en: takes the ground painted with it along

paint.swatch_move_to.note: The colour dialogue: the option that moves the colour to another layer; {layer} is the layer's name.

paint.swatch_remove.note: The colour dialogue: the option that deletes the colour.

paint.swatch_remove_body.en: {label}: the ground painted with it goes back to whatever rule its ground texture would have used.
paint.swatch_remove_body.note: That dialogue's body; {label} is the colour.

paint.swatch_remove_title.note: Heading of the dialogue confirming a colour's removal.

paint.swatch_repoint.note: The colour dialogue for a rule colour: the option that changes which rule it stands for.

paint.swatch_repoint_note.en: the ground you painted stays where it is

paint.these_cells.note: Under the option that clears one colour in view.

paint.this_interior.note: The clear-in-view dialogues, standing in for an interior with no name.

paint.this_object.note: The crowded-mesh dialogue: what to call an object with no mesh path.

paint.where_cells.en: the {n} cells the viewport is showing
paint.where_cells.note: The clear-in-view dialogues, the "where" when several cells are loaded; {n} is how many.

paint.where_preview.note: The colour dialogue's list of cells a colour is painted in: the button on each row.

paint.where_preview_title.note: That button's tooltip; {cell} is the row's cell.

panel.add_ban.note: Right panel, the bans section: the button that adds an empty ban.

panel.add_meshes.note: Right column, the button that adds several meshes at once.

panel.add_meshes_tip.en: Pick several .nif files at once and add one slot per mesh
panel.add_meshes_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Add meshes button.

panel.add_slot.note: Right column, the button that adds a grass card.

panel.additive.note: Right column, the Adds to the ground label under Scope, shown for a scoped rule.

panel.additive_hint_off.en: Replaces: inside this scope, only this rule scatters on the texture. This is how a scoped rule has always worked.
panel.additive_hint_off.note: Right column, under the Adds to the ground switch while it is off.

panel.additive_hint_on.en: Adds: this rule scatters on top of the texture's other rules (for example reeds on a coast that keeps its grass). Each rule packs on its own, so the ground gets denser where they overlap.
panel.additive_hint_on.note: Right column, under the Adds to the ground switch while it is on.

panel.additive_tip.en: Off: inside its scope this rule replaces the texture's other rules. On: it scatters beside them inside its scope, without removing any of them. A Gardenfell addition.
panel.additive_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Adds to the ground label.

panel.align.note: Right column, the Follow ground slope label.

panel.align_tip.en: bAlignObjectNormalToGround: tilts each object to follow the ground slope
panel.align_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Follow ground slope label.

panel.ban_all.note: The Exclusions section, in a multi-edit: the button that replaces every selected rule's exclusions with one pasted list.

panel.ban_all_apply.note: The paste-to-all dialogue's confirming button. {n} is how many rules are selected.

panel.ban_all_head.note: The paste-to-all dialogue's heading. {n} is how many rules are selected.

panel.ban_all_note.en: All {n} selected rules get exactly this list. Their current exclusions are replaced, not added to. One undo step puts it all back.
panel.ban_all_note.note: The paste-to-all dialogue's note under the box. {n} is how many rules are selected.

panel.ban_all_title.en: Paste one list of exclusions to all {n} selected rules, replacing their current lists
panel.ban_all_title.note: The Exclusions section: that button's tooltip. {n} is how many rules are selected.

panel.ban_del_title.note: Right panel, a ban row: the delete button's tooltip.

panel.ban_fade.note: Right panel, under a ban: the switch that shrinks grass towards the cleared ring.

panel.ban_fade_dist_tip.en: How far the shrinking runs, in units, measured out from the edge of the cleared ring
panel.ban_fade_dist_tip.note: The fade row: the distance field's tooltip.

panel.ban_fade_down_to.note: Right panel, the fade row: the words between the distance and the minimum size.

panel.ban_fade_min_tip.en: Size of the grass at the edge of the cleared ring, as a fraction of full size
panel.ban_fade_min_tip.note: The fade row: the minimum-size field's tooltip.

panel.ban_fade_over.note: Right panel, the fade row: the word before the distance field ("Fade grass over N u, down to M").

panel.ban_io.note: Right panel, the bans section: the button that opens the ban list as text.

panel.ban_io_empty.en: This rule has no bans yet. Paste some in.
panel.ban_io_empty.note: The ban list dialogue: the note when the rule has no bans.

panel.ban_io_head.note: The ban list dialogue's heading; {rule} is the rule's texture.

panel.ban_io_hint.en: Written in the Groundcover Generator .ini's spelling, so this pastes into another rule here or into one of those .ini files. It does not paste into a Gardenfell .toml, which writes bans differently. Bare texture names and name = offset lines are accepted too.
panel.ban_io_hint.note: The ban list dialogue: the hint over the text area.

panel.ban_io_title.en: Copy this ban list, or paste one in from another section or an .ini

panel.ban_offer_cell.en: Also painted in this cell. Click to ban:
panel.ban_offer_cell.note: Right panel, the bans section: the label over the offered textures in Real cell mode.

panel.ban_offer_patch.en: Also on this patch. Click to ban:
panel.ban_offer_patch.note: Right panel, the bans section: the label over the offered textures in Simplified mode.

panel.ban_offer_pct.note: The offered-texture button's tooltip: how much of the cell the texture covers, before the "add" part.

panel.ban_placeholder.note: Right panel, a ban row: the texture field's placeholder.

panel.band.note: Right column, the Between label on a Terrain band.

panel.band_tip.en: Low, high, fade, in {unit}. Leave a side empty to leave it open.
panel.band_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Between label on a Terrain band.

panel.bans_added.one.note: Toast after the ban list dialogue appended to the list.

panel.bans_added.other.note: Toast after the ban list dialogue appended to the list.

panel.bans_hint.en: Ground more than half covered by a banned texture gets no grass. The offset keeps grass that many units clear of it.
panel.bans_hint.note: Right column, at the foot of the Exclusions section.

panel.bans_hint_title.en: Land textures blend into each other, so grass can land on ground that is mostly road. Turn on Ban strip in Simplified to preview how a ban clears a road.

panel.bans_replaced.one.note: Toast after the ban list dialogue replaced the list.

panel.bans_replaced.other.note: Toast after the ban list dialogue replaced the list.

panel.bans_replaced_all.one.note: Toast after pasting one list of exclusions over a multi-edit selection, singular. {rules} is how many rules took it.

panel.bans_replaced_all.other.note: Toast after pasting a list of exclusions over a multi-edit selection. {rules} is how many rules took it.

panel.bulk_bans_differ.en: Different exclusions, can't edit several at the same time
panel.bulk_bans_differ.note: Right column, in place of the exclusions when the selected rules carry different ones.

panel.bulk_identity_hint.en: The ground texture and scope are kept per rule and edited one rule at a time. Everything below this is edited for all of them at once.
panel.bulk_identity_hint.note: Right column, under the list of rules when several are selected.

panel.bulk_slots_differ.en: Different grass slots, can't edit several at the same time
panel.bulk_slots_differ.note: Right column, in place of the grass cards when the selected rules carry different ones.

panel.bulk_slots_hint.en: Select rules with the same grass slots to edit them together.

panel.cell.note: Right column, the Cell / region label.

panel.cell_hint_offline.en: The file format does not distinguish a cell from a region, so the generator tries cell name first, then region name. Case does not matter, and most Morrowind regions end in  Region (e.g. Bitter Coast Region). Connect your install to get a checked list.
panel.cell_hint_offline.note: Right column, under Cell / region with no install connected.

panel.cell_hint_painted.en: The list only shows where {texture} is painted: {regions} region(s) and {cells} named cell(s), read from the landscape. Anywhere else would scatter nothing.
panel.cell_hint_painted.note: Right column, under Cell / region when the texture is painted somewhere. {texture}, {regions} and {cells} are filled in.

panel.cell_hint_wide.en: The file format does not distinguish a cell from a region, so the generator tries cell name first, then region name. The list offers {regions} region(s) and {cells} named exterior cell(s) from your load order{tail}
panel.cell_hint_wide.note: Right column, under Cell / region when the texture is not painted anywhere yet. {regions} and {cells} count the whole load order; {tail} is one of the two lines below.

panel.cell_hint_wide_done.en: , though this texture was not found painted anywhere.
panel.cell_hint_wide_done.note: Right column, the end of the line above once the landscape has been read.

panel.cell_hint_wide_pending.en: . The landscape pass will narrow it per texture.
panel.cell_hint_wide_pending.note: Right column, the end of the same line while the landscape is still being read.

panel.cell_tip.en: Tried as a cell name first, then as a region name
panel.cell_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Cell / region label.

panel.clump.note: Right column, the Clump meshes label.

panel.clump_hint.en: Pair it with a heavy Empty slot to get sparse clusters (like a flower field) instead of even coverage.
panel.clump_hint.note: Right column, under the Clump meshes switch.

panel.clump_tip.en: bRandClump: one mesh per patch of ground instead of a random mesh per blade
panel.clump_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Clump meshes label.

panel.clumping_hint.en: A Gardenfell addition. Groundcover Generator has no key for it, so it is saved in the rules file and affects both the preview and the export. A plain groundcover .ini read in another tool goes back to even scatter.
panel.clumping_hint.note: Right column, at the top of the Organic clumping section.

panel.clumping_hint2.en: Patches are anchored to the world, so they run across cell borders rather than restarting at each one.
panel.clumping_hint2.note: Right column, at the foot of the Organic clumping section.

panel.clumping_on.note: Right column, the Enabled label under Organic clumping.

panel.clumping_on_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Enabled label.

panel.clumpnoise.note: Right column, the Noisy clumps label.

panel.clumpnoise_hint.en: Gives the clumps uneven outlines instead of square ones. Nothing else changes: same blades, same positions, only which mesh each one gets.
panel.clumpnoise_hint.note: Right column, under the Noisy clumps switch.

panel.clumpnoise_tip.en: A Gardenfell addition. Off by default so an imported .ini keeps its square tiling.
panel.clumpnoise_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Noisy clumps label.

panel.clumpsize.note: Right column, the Clump size label.

panel.clumpsize_hint.en: A land texture tile is 512 units, so 512 is the default. Clumps are anchored to the world, so they run across cell borders and stay in place when you change the gap.
panel.clumpsize_hint.note: Right column, under the Clump size field.

panel.clumpsize_tip.en: iClumpArea: how much ground one mesh covers, in units
panel.clumpsize_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Clump size label.

panel.copied_slot.note: The paste toast's {name} when the card has neither mesh nor id.

panel.cover_tip.en: How much of the eligible ground keeps grass
panel.cover_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Coverage label.

panel.curve_hint.en: "Below −20" scatters only in hollows. "Above 20" scatters only on ridges.
panel.curve_hint.note: Right column, under the Curvature fields while it is on.

panel.curve_hint_off.note: Right column, under the Curvature switch while it is off.

panel.curve_radius.note: Right column, the Measured over label under Curvature.

panel.curve_radius_tip.en: How far out to measure, in units. 512 is one land texture tile. 128 is the finest the landscape grid goes.
panel.curve_radius_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Measured over label.

panel.curve_tip.en: Hollow or ridge: how far the ground here stands above the average of the ground around it. Negative is a hollow, positive a ridge.
panel.curve_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Curvature label.

panel.edge.note: Right column, the Edge softness label.

panel.edge_tip.en: 0 gives a hard edge, higher lets the patch edges fray
panel.edge_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Edge softness label.

panel.even.note: Right column, the button that levels every weight.

panel.even_tip.en: Set every slot to the same chance
panel.even_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Even weights button.

panel.facing_at.note: Right column, the Heading label under Facing.

panel.facing_at_tip.en: Compass degrees: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west. Then how far either side still counts, and a fade in degrees.
panel.facing_at_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Heading label.

panel.facing_hint.en: A slope faces the direction it drops.
panel.facing_hint.note: Right column, under the Facing fields while it is on.

panel.facing_hint_off.note: Right column, under the Facing switch while it is off.

panel.facing_reads.en: Reads as: slopes facing {dir}, from {from}° round to {to}°.
panel.facing_reads.note: Right column, the sentence under the Facing fields that says the heading in words.

panel.facing_tip.en: Only scatters on slopes that face a chosen compass direction. Flat ground always passes. Raise Shallowest slope to keep grass off flat ground.
panel.facing_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Facing label.

panel.fade_tip.en: Fade: how far past the limit the grass thins out and shrinks instead of stopping. 0 is a hard cut.
panel.fade_tip.note: Right column, hovering any fade field.

panel.gap_hint.en: Smaller means denser. Keep it under 512.
panel.gap_hint.note: Right column, under the Gap field.

panel.gap_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Gap label.

panel.gate_mixed.en: These rules disagree here. Switch it either way to set them all.
panel.gate_mixed.note: Right column, under a Terrain switch when several rules are edited together and disagree.

panel.height_hint.en: The sea is at 0, so a Lowest ground just above it keeps grass out of the water. Red tint marks ground these settings reject.
panel.height_hint.note: Right column, under the Culling fields.

panel.jitter.note: Right column, the Jitter label under Gap.

panel.jitter_hint.en: Each object may move up to {pct}% of the gap, but never closer than {floor}% of the gap to a neighbor, and never onto ground its rule would refuse (roads, rocks, wrong texture). Breaks up the rows a sparse scatter falls into. The number of objects does not change.
panel.jitter_hint.note: Right column, under the Jitter slider while it is above zero.

panel.jitter_hint_mixed.en: These rules disagree about jitter. Move the slider to set them all.
panel.jitter_hint_mixed.note: Right column, under the Jitter slider when several rules are edited together and disagree.

panel.jitter_hint_off.en: Off: every object stays exactly where the packing put it. At a high gap that looks like rows. Turn this up to break them.
panel.jitter_hint_off.note: Right column, under the Jitter slider while it is at zero.

panel.jitter_tip.en: Moves each object off the spot the packing chose, by up to this fraction of the gap. A Gardenfell addition, with no .ini key.
panel.jitter_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Jitter label.

panel.maxh.note: Right column, the Highest ground label.

panel.maxh_tip.en: fMaxHeight: no grass above this height
panel.maxh_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Highest ground label.

panel.minh.note: Right column, the Lowest ground label.

panel.minh_tip.en: fMinHeight: no grass below this height
panel.minh_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Lowest ground label.

panel.notes_ph.en: e.g. bulk of the landscape, 43 uses
panel.notes_ph.note: Right column, the grey text in the Notes box.

panel.notes_tip.en: Kept with the rule in the config, and read from the ; comments above a section when an .ini is imported
panel.notes_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Notes label.

panel.obstacle.note: Right column, the Near objects label in the Terrain section (round 18k).

panel.obstacle_hint.en: "0 to 64" scatters only close to objects, like moss around rocks and along walls. "128 and up" keeps grass back from everything. A grass card can set a tighter value for itself.
panel.obstacle_hint.note: Right column, under the Near objects fields while it is on.

panel.obstacle_hint_off.note: Right column, under the Near objects switch while it is off.

panel.obstacle_tip.en: Distance from the nearest object, the same objects that obstacle avoidance uses, measured from their surface in three dimensions. A bridge overhead counts as far away as it is high. Works with obstacle avoidance off as well.
panel.obstacle_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Near objects label.

panel.paint_only.note: Right column, the switch that detaches a rule from any ground texture.

panel.paint_only_hint.en: Never scatters on a ground texture by itself. Give it a color under Paint tools and paint ground with it, and this rule scatters there, whatever land texture is underneath. Its own slope, height and exclusions still apply.
panel.paint_only_hint.note: Right column, under the name of a paint-only rule.

panel.paint_only_tip.en: This rule has no land texture. It only scatters on ground you paint with its color.
panel.paint_only_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Paint only rule label.

panel.paste_slot.note: Right panel, the grass slots section: the button that pastes the copied card; {name} is its mesh or id.

panel.paste_slot_title.en: Add the copied grass card to this texture

panel.patchwidth.note: Right column, the Patch width label.

panel.patchwidth_tip.en: How wide one patch of grass runs. 8192 is a whole cell.
panel.patchwidth_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Patch width label.

panel.place.note: Right column, the Place grass label.

panel.place_off_hint.en: This is an exclusion rule: it places nothing, and it stops a broader rule from placing anything here either. Useful as a pair: this one scoped to named cells and switched off, a plain one switched on.
panel.place_off_hint.note: Right column, shown when Place grass is off.

panel.place_tip.en: bPlaceGrass: on or off for this whole rule
panel.place_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Place grass label.

panel.rule_name.note: Right column, the name field that replaces Ground texture on a paint-only rule.

panel.rule_name_tip.en: Name of this rule. Any name works, it is never looked up in your install.
panel.rule_name_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Rule name label.

panel.scl_off_hint.en: Every object is placed at the smallest size. A slot with its own range still uses that.
panel.scl_off_hint.note: Right column, under the scale range when varying is off.

panel.scl_on_hint.en: Each object gets a random size from this range. A slot can override it. Set both ends the same for a fixed size.
panel.scl_on_hint.note: Right column, under the scale range when varying is on.

panel.sclrand.note: Right column, the Vary the scale label.

panel.sclrand_tip.en: bSclRand: off places every object at the smallest size instead of a random one
panel.sclrand_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Vary the scale label.

panel.sclrange.note: Right column, the Scale range label.

panel.sclrange_tip.en: fSclMin / fSclMax: smallest and largest size
panel.sclrange_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Scale range label.

panel.scope_everywhere.note: Right column, the first Scope choice.

panel.scope_named.en: Only cells that have a name (ANY_NAMED_CELL)
panel.scope_named.note: Right column, the second Scope choice.

panel.scope_specific.note: Right column, the third Scope choice.

panel.scope_tip.en: How this section is narrowed down
panel.scope_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Scope label.

panel.sec_bans.note: Right panel: the bans section's heading (with several rules selected).

panel.sec_bans_n.note: Right panel: the bans section's heading, with the count.

panel.sec_clumping.note: Right panel: the clumping section's heading; {state} is on, off or — when the rules differ.

panel.sec_culling.note: Right column, the heading of the Culling section.

panel.sec_placement.note: Right column, the heading of the Placement section.

panel.sec_random.note: Right column, the heading of the Randomisation section.

panel.sec_selector.note: Right column, the heading of the first section.

panel.sec_slots.note: Right panel: the grass slots section's heading (with several rules selected).

panel.sec_slots_n.note: Right panel: the grass slots section's heading, with the count.

panel.sec_terrain.note: Right column, the heading of the Terrain section.

panel.shore_align.note: Right column, the switch under the Shoreline fields (round 18k).

panel.shore_align_tip.en: Lays every blade along the water's edge instead of rotating it at random: its X axis runs along the shore and its +Y faces the water. Meant for meshes that are longer than they are wide, like reeds and driftwood, which look wrong at a random angle on a coast. Only where the ground slopes. Flat ground keeps the random rotation.
panel.shore_align_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Rotate with shoreline switch.

panel.shore_hint.en: "0 to 300" gives a strip along the coast. "100 and up" keeps grass back from the water. "Below 0" scatters only under water. Height alone cannot follow a coastline, this can.
panel.shore_hint.note: Right column, under the Shoreline fields while it is on.

panel.shore_hint_off.en: Off: any distance from the water.
panel.shore_hint_off.note: Right column, under the Shoreline switch while it is off.

panel.shore_tip.en: Distance from where the land meets the water, in units. Negative is under water. Exteriors only: interior water does not count as a shoreline.
panel.shore_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Shoreline label.

panel.shore_turn.note: Right column, the Turn label under Rotate with shoreline.

panel.shore_turn_tip.en: Degrees added on top, for a mesh modeled the other way round. 90 turns it a quarter, 180 faces it away from the water.
panel.shore_turn_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Turn label.

panel.slope.note: Right column, the Steepest slope label.

panel.slope_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Steepest slope label.

panel.slopemin.note: Right column, the Shallowest slope label.

panel.slopemin_tip.en: Ground flatter than this, in degrees, gets no grass. Second field: degrees of fade below it. A Gardenfell addition.
panel.slopemin_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Shallowest slope label.

panel.slot_pasted.note: Toast after pasting a grass card onto a rule.

panel.slot_word.note: The paste-card button's {name} when the copied card has neither mesh nor id.

panel.slots_added.note: Toast after Add meshes made a slot per chosen mesh.

panel.slots_hint.en: Weights, not percentages. They do not need to add up to anything. A slot is either a mesh or an object ID from another plugin, never both.
panel.slots_hint.note: Right column, under the grass cards.

panel.state_off.note: A section heading's state word: the feature is off.

panel.state_on.note: A section heading's state word: the feature is on.

panel.terrain_hint.en: Rules based on the terrain where the grass would stand: which way it faces, whether it is a hollow or a ridge, how far the water is. Each is off until switched on, and costs nothing while off.
panel.terrain_hint.note: Right column, under the Terrain heading.

panel.tex.note: Right column, the Land texture label.

panel.tex_tip.en: The LTEX id as it appears in the game data. Case does not matter.
panel.tex_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Land texture label.

panel.tex_unknown.en: This id matches no LTEX record in the scanned load order, so this section will never place anything. Check the spelling and case, or enable the plugin that defines it.
panel.tex_unknown.note: Right column, when the land texture is not in the load order.

panel.warp_tip.en: 0 gives round blobs, higher gives winding shapes
panel.warp_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Warp label.

panel.zoff.note: Right column, the per-rule height offset label.

panel.zoff_hint.en: Moves this texture's grass up or down. 0 is not ground level: Groundcover Generator lifts everything it places by 16 units, and this is added on top, so an imported .ini keeps its meaning. Use −16 to place exactly on the ground. A mesh modeled around its middle needs a different value from one modeled from its base, which is why it is per rule rather than per file.
panel.zoff_hint.note: Right column, under the Height offset field.

panel.zoff_tip.en: iZPositionModifier: added on top of the 16 units Groundcover Generator always adds
panel.zoff_tip.note: Right column, hovering the Height offset label.

plugins.all.note: The plugin chooser: ticks everything the filter is showing.

plugins.from_install.note: The end of that note on a fresh connect, when the ticks came from the load order.

plugins.from_loaded.en: Ticked to match what is loaded right now. Back to install returns to your load order.
plugins.from_loaded.note: The end of that note when the chooser was reopened on an install already loaded.

plugins.hint.en: Every plugin your install has is listed, switched on or not. Untick what you do not want loaded. A plugin something else needs as a master stays, shown with a dash, until the thing that needs it is unticked too. Nothing here is saved, you are asked each time.
plugins.hint.note: The plugin chooser's note, under the heading.

plugins.n_as_masters.one.en: {n} of them only because something else needs it
plugins.n_as_masters.one.note: Under the plugin chooser's list, for exactly one.

plugins.n_as_masters.other.en: {n} of them only because something else needs them
plugins.n_as_masters.other.note: Under the plugin chooser's list; {n} is how many are loaded only as masters.

plugins.n_of.note: The plugin chooser's count; {n} is how many will load, {total} how many it could.

plugins.n_shown.note: Under the plugin chooser's list when a filter is hiding some; {n} is how many are visible.

plugins.needed_by.note: The plugin chooser, beside a row that is loaded only because something else rests on it.

plugins.none.note: The plugin chooser: unticks everything the filter is showing.

plugins.none_as_masters.en: Every one of them ticked in its own right.
plugins.none_as_masters.note: Under the plugin chooser's list when nothing is loaded only as a master.

plugins.not_found.note: The plugin chooser, beside a plugin the load order names and the install does not have.

plugins.not_on.note: The plugin chooser, beside a plugin the install has but its load order does not name.

plugins.probe_failed.en: Could not read the load order to ask which plugins to load, so all of them are being loaded: {err}
plugins.probe_failed.note: A warning when the plugin chooser's probe failed; the install is opened whole instead.

plugins.reset.note: The plugin chooser: ticks exactly what the install has switched on, ignoring the filter.

plugins.reset_title.en: Tick exactly what your install has switched on (the state this dialog opened in). Unlike Tick all, this ignores the filter.

plugins.unreadable.note: The plugin chooser, beside a plugin that is there but whose header could not be read.

preview.adjacent_title.en: How far out from the chosen cell the landscape and its objects are loaded

preview.base_title.en: The height above the water level the terrain is placed at

preview.dof_title.en: Depth of field similar to MGE XE options. Focus point is on whatever is at the middle of the screen

preview.fogd_from.note: Left column, on the sources line after Reset to install — before the file the fog distances came from.

preview.fogd_reset_title.en: Reset to what your install says: MGE XE's own distances for the weather, read from mge3\MGE.ini when you have one.

preview.fogd_title.en: 100 is MGE XE's own distance for this weather.

preview.fpscap_title.en: Never draw the viewport faster than the number below

preview.fpsmax_title.en: The most frames per second the viewport may draw while the cap is toggled on

preview.full_note.en: the whole patch, no fade at the edge

preview.full_title.en: Render the ground texture to the edge of the terrain or not. Used to see how grass fades at the edge of a texture.

preview.fxaa_title.en: Fast approximate anti-aliasing. Smooths the edges multisampling leaves, at some softness

preview.grassfar_cells.one.note: Viewport, the grass distance pill: the slider's value.

preview.grassfar_cells.other.note: Viewport, the grass distance pill: the slider's value.

preview.grassfar_title.en: How far from the camera grass is drawn, in cells. Preview only: the plugin still gets every blade. No limit draws all grass always, which is slow with many cells loaded.

preview.hint.en: Changes only what you see, never the plugin.

preview.hour_title.en: The game hour. Sunrise and sunset are read from your Morrowind.ini.

preview.invented_hint.en: Terrain to simulate different conditions in the game and preview different culling rules.

preview.lights_title.en: Whether the cell's lamps are lit. Night time is on from 18:00 to 07:00.

preview.mge_title.en: The blades lit and cut out similar to how MGE XE G7’s branch’s grass shader does it. Off draws them as any placed object.

preview.mgew_title.en: The water as MGE XE's water shader draws it. Off is a plain translucent sheet.

preview.mode_hint_cell.en: The real landscape and every placed object. Slower, but the only way to see clipping.
preview.mode_hint_cell.note: Left column, under the mode picker while Real cell is chosen.

preview.mode_hint_simple.en: Terrain patch: Good for judging density and clustering.
preview.mode_hint_simple.note: Left column, under the mode picker while Simplified is chosen.

preview.particles_title.en: When on, particle systems render as they do in-game. Torches and lamps only emit if the light is on.

preview.pause_still_title.en: While the camera is not moving, nothing is redrawn. Less work for your hardware, but no animated water, particles etc.

preview.relief_title.en: Goes from flat slab to hilly

preview.renderer_att.en: [LightAttenuation] from {file}: constant {c}, linear {l}, quadratic {q} (a 256-unit lamp: c {c256}, l {l256}, q {q256})
preview.renderer_att.note: Hover text on the sources line — the light attenuation settings read, the file they came from, and the coefficients they give a 256-unit lamp.

preview.renderer_att_default.en: [LightAttenuation] not in {file}: the game's shipped values (linear 3/r)
preview.renderer_att_default.note: Hover text on the sources line — no [LightAttenuation] section was found, so the shipped values are used.

preview.renderer_model_ffp.en: fixed pipeline (per vertex in the game): 1/(c + l·d + q·d²) per lamp, the sum clamped to white.
preview.renderer_model_ffp.note: Hover text on the sources line — what the fixed-pipeline lighting model is (vanilla, MGE with per-pixel lighting off, OpenMW's legacy method).

preview.renderer_model_mge.en: MGE XE per-pixel lighting: 1/(q·d² + c) per lamp, with the linear term dropped as in its shader. The lit color is tonemapped, not clamped. Grass takes sun and ambient only.
preview.renderer_model_mge.note: Hover text on the sources line — what the MGE lighting model is.

preview.renderer_model_openmw.en: OpenMW shaders: 1/(c + l·d + q·d²) per lamp, capped at 1, faded out between {bounds}× the radius and twice that.
preview.renderer_model_openmw.note: Hover text on the sources line — what the OpenMW shader lighting model is; {bounds} is its light bounds multiplier.

preview.renderer_post.note: Hover text on the sources line — the post-process shaders the install's chain names that the preview has an answer for (SSAO, sunshafts…), or 'none'.

preview.renderer_wow.en: Wonders of Water: under the surface the fog's start and end are × max(1 − depth/{units}, {min}) and the water's color × (1 − depth/{units}). Settings from {file}.
preview.renderer_wow.note: Hover text on the sources line — what Wonders of Water does to the underwater fog, and which config it was read from.

preview.renderer_wow_defaults.en: the mod's own defaults (no Wonders of Water.json in the overwrite folder)
preview.renderer_wow_defaults.note: Hover text on the sources line — where Wonders of Water's settings came from when no config file was found.

preview.renderer_wow_off.en: Wonders of Water is installed but not acting: it is disabled or its depth-based clarity is off in {file}, or this install does not run MWSE on MGE XE.
preview.renderer_wow_off.note: Hover text on the sources line — Wonders of Water was found but the preview does not follow it, and why.

preview.rules_here_hint.en: Shows all rules acting on the same ground texture. Switches toggle on and off rules for the preview only.

preview.shadows_title.en: The sun's shadows as MGE XE draws them. Cast by the terrain, placed objects and anything moving among them, never by grass (the game does not cast shadows from grass either).

preview.shore_title.en: Put the terrain back at a little above water level.

preview.sky_room.en: Off in interiors: an interior has no sky unless its cell is flagged to behave like an exterior. Your setting comes back when you leave.
preview.sky_room.note: Left column, the tooltip on the dimmed Atmosphere row while an interior is up.

preview.sky_src.note: Left column, under the Weather picker — the lead-in before the list of files the sky's colours were read from.

preview.sky_src_builtin.en: no weather in the ini, using default values
preview.sky_src_builtin.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — the ini or openmw.cfg had no [Weather] blocks.

preview.sky_src_mge2.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — fog distances, and the file they were read from (mgeXE.toml or mge3\MGE.ini).

preview.sky_src_mge_default.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — no MGE.ini, MGE XE's built-in fog distances.

preview.sky_src_mge_how.en: how the fog file was chosen: {how}
preview.sky_src_mge_how.note: Left column, the title (hover text) on the sources line — why that MGE config file was the one read.

preview.sky_src_none.en: Sky: using default values, until an install is connected.
preview.sky_src_none.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows while nothing is connected.

preview.sky_src_renderer.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — the renderer whose lighting model the preview follows, by its own name (e.g. 'MGE-XE G7 Fork v0.20.0', 'OpenMW', 'Morrowind.exe, no MGE').

preview.sky_src_wow.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — the MWSE mod Wonders of Water is installed and its depth rule is followed under the water.

preview.sky_title.en: The game's sky, sun and haze, drawn MGE XE's way. Off is the plain backdrop and the flat fog.

preview.ssao_title.en: Darkens areas where meshes meet to simulate sun light bouncing and losing strength the further into crevices they go

preview.statics_forced_title.note: Left column, Preview: the Draw objects row's tooltip while an interior forces it on.

preview.strip_no_ban.en: This rule bans no texture, so there is no strip to draw. Add one under Bans.
preview.strip_no_ban.note: Toast (once) when the road strip is on but the rule has no bans.

preview.strip_note.en: a band of this rule's own banned texture

preview.strip_other_plugin.en: The banned texture comes from a different plugin than this one, so the two cannot share a cell. The strip is left out.
preview.strip_other_plugin.note: Toast (once) when the banned texture cannot be drawn on the patch.

preview.strip_title.en: Requires a ban texture in the grass rule. Make a strip through the terrain patch of the first banned texture to show how the rule culls grass.

preview.texdetail_title.en: The largest size a texture is loaded at. Using mips for smaller textures. Set low to save on performance.

preview.timeflow_title.en: Progresses the Time of day automatically

preview.timescale_title.en: Amount of minutes per real second

preview.tint_title.en: How much of the ground's color a blade takes at its base, fading to its own color at the tip. Does not affect the exported .esp.

preview.under_title.en: Similar to MGE XE’s underwater effects when using popular shaders. Fog distances and light reflect your install, including if you use Wonders of Water.

preview.unlit_title.en: Shows meshes with base brightness, unaffected by light (especially good if a place is very dark)

preview.wind_title.en: How much the grass sways. Does not affect the exported .esp.

unmatched.all_good.en: Every rule resolves against your current load order.

unmatched.go.note: The unmatched-rules dialogue: the button beside each row.

unmatched.go_field_title.en: Closes this and selects [{rule}] in the rules list and flashes the {field} field. Nothing is changed.
unmatched.go_field_title.note: That button's tooltip for a name that was not found; {field} is the field's name (texture, scope…).

unmatched.go_mesh_title.note: That button's tooltip for a missing mesh.

unmatched.how.en: Each line is one rule and the name it could not find. Take me to entry closes this, selects that rule in the list and flashes the field the problem is in: the grass card for a missing mesh, the name or scope field otherwise. Nothing on this dialog changes your config.
unmatched.how.note: The unmatched-rules dialogue: the note explaining the list.

unmatched.meshes.en: ⚠ {n} mesh(es) are not in your install. Those grass cards take positions and draw nothing. In the viewport the positions are marked, and in the export the objects are written pointing at a file the game cannot load. Mesh paths are matched without regard to case, so the file is missing rather than misspelled. Install the mod it comes from, or point the card at something else.
unmatched.meshes.note: The unmatched-rules dialogue: the box over the missing meshes.

unmatched.names.en: {n} name(s) will place nothing. Nothing in your load order is called this, in any capitalization, so it is a misspelling, or a plugin that defines it is not enabled. A rule that matches nothing places nothing without warning, which is why this list exists.
unmatched.names.note: The unmatched-rules dialogue: the box over the names that were not found.

unmatched.no_install.en: No install is connected, so there is nothing to check these names against.
unmatched.no_install.note: The unmatched-rules dialogue before a setup is connected.

vp.back_to_preview.note: Viewport: the button that leaves the mesh editor.

vp.light_title.en: Change brightness of lights in the scene preview. Default is 100%
